questions.question: DDIA’s home-timeline SQL sketch joins posts to follow relationships to:
options: Charge every user a fee before showing ads only.
Fetch recent posts from people the user follows.
Delete all followers older than one day automatically.
Convert the social graph into a CDN edge certificate.
questions.explanation: home timeline, which displays recent posts by people the user is following

questions.question: Fan-out on write means:
options: Computing the feed only when the user opens the app.
Pushing a new post into followers’ feed caches/stores at write time.
Never storing posts so feeds are always empty.
Writing the post only to the author’s profile and never to followers.

questions.question: Celebrity users break naive fan-out-on-write because:
options: They have so many followers that write amplification explodes.
They are not allowed to post more than one byte of text.
Databases refuse to store posts from verified accounts.
Load balancers drop packets only for famous accounts.
questions.explanation: a few celebrities… have over 100 million followers

questions.question: Polling the timeline query every few seconds for millions online users:
options: Is free because SQL joins never cost CPU.
Can create enormous read QPS and expensive joins - hence caching/fan-out designs.
Is required by the HTTP specification for all social apps.
Removes the need for indexes on follow tables.
questions.explanation: running the query 2 million times per second… This query is also quite expensive
